task_title: AI Sweep resume rebuild + legacy runInputs inference

plan_review.notes: Retroactive plan review, triggered by copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot] correctly identifying this diff (8 files, ~1560 insertions across .github/workflows/ai-sweep.yml, scripts/agent/perf/round-plan.ts, scripts/agent/perf/sweep-eval.ts, and 2 test files) as 3 apples, not the originally-declared 2. Reviewed the cross-run resume design (resume_run_id workflow_dispatch input, resume-import job, assertResumeCompatible/inferRunInputsFromCheckpoint/extractLegacyBaselineShard, round-boundary resume granularity) against two alternatives -- strict same-workflow-SHA-only resume, and salvaging in-flight round shards instead of whole-round-tier resume -- both rejected for the reasons documented in the PR body/handoff. BLOCKING finding: baseline and checkpoint-init jobs' if: conditions gated only on needs.resume-import.outputs.hasFreshCombos, not on resume-import's own job result. A custom job-level if: REPLACES (does not AND with) GitHub Actions' implicit success() gate, so a resume-import job that fails after its 'Select latest compatible checkpoint' step has already written hasFreshCombos/freshCombos/resumedCombos (e.g. a later 'Upload resumed checkpoints bundle' step failing) could still let baseline/checkpoint-init proceed on stale/incomplete resume state. FIXED: added `needs.resume-import.result == 'success'` to both jobs' if: conditions, plus a dedicated regression test in tests/unit/ai-sweep-workflow.test.ts. Legacy-runInputs inference (complete/duplicate-free/rectangular baseline-panel requirement, exact secondary key-set match, workflowSha deliberately excluded from provenance) and round-boundary-only resume granularity (no partial-round shard salvage) were both assessed as sound and correctly the smallest-correct design for the declared scope cap.

rounds.notes: Reviewed assertResumeCompatible/inferRunInputsFromCheckpoint/normalizeResumedCheckpoint/extractLegacyBaselineShard in round-plan.ts, the resume-import/baseline/checkpoint-init wiring in ai-sweep.yml (including the needs.resume-import.result == success fix from the plan-review round), and test coverage in both spec files. npx tsc --noEmit clean; targeted vitest run (tests/unit/ai/sweep-round-plan.test.ts + tests/unit/ai-sweep-workflow.test.ts) green. No new concerns raised; independently confirmed the plan-review DAG-gating fix is applied to exactly the two places it is needed (baseline, checkpoint-init) and that round1/round2/round3-select jobs correctly do NOT need the same guard, since they consume preflight.outputs.combos rather than resume-imports freshCombos/hasFreshCombos outputs.

Follow-up round after PR #1759 was briefly closed (superseded by standalone PR #1760) then reopened by explicit human override (I want generic resume capability). Merged latest main (bringing in #1735 net-win promotion + #1760, both unaffected by this PRs files) and addressed 3 remaining copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot] threads: (1) normalizeResumedCheckpoint re-stamps meta.workflowSha to the CURRENT runs value on an accepted resumed checkpoint -- previously left the PRIOR runs sha in place, which would fail every downstream same-run provenance check (applyRoundResult, initCheckpoint, aggregate-shards.ts) once the resuming commit -- by construction -- carries a different sha; (2) resume-check tier scan now bounded by a $TIERS case-statement keyed on inputs.rounds instead of an unconditional r3>r2>r1>init scan; continue-on-error removed from legacy-baseline-derivation so a derivation failure fails the job hard; SECONDARY_KNOBS detection fixed from unsound .some() to all-or-none, matching production knobsForCombo exactly; (3) --print-meta default stage and evalStandalones stamped meta.stage were independently-literal search strings with no compiler-enforced link (a real latent drift risk, though not a live bug today) -- extracted to one exported STANDALONE_SHARD_STAGE constant used by both call sites, plus a pinning regression test. All 3 verified via targeted tests (158/158 across sweep-round-plan/ai-sweep-workflow/sweep-eval-search-promotion) and npx tsc --noEmit clean. Also recorded apple calibration (estimated 2 -> actual 3, verdict Under) per a 4th bot thread noting the ledgers already-declared 3-apple tier was not reflected in the handoff. Additionally fixed a 5th bot-flagged bug: --mode init previously silently dropped BOTH --train-seeds/--weapons when only one was supplied, producing an unintended legacy-style checkpoint; extracted an exported, independently-tested resolveInitRunInputs helper that now throws on the one-present/one-missing case (4 new tests). Final targeted count: 162/162.

6th bot-flagged bug surfaced in a fresh copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot] pass immediately after the round-2 push: the resume-import job's 'Upload resumed checkpoints bundle' step ran BEFORE the 'Derive legacy+legacy baseline shard'/'Upload derived legacy+legacy baseline shard' steps. Because a step failure without continue-on-error only skips LATER steps in the same job, resumed-checkpoints was already durably uploaded before a later legacy-baseline derivation/upload failure could occur -- so a hard-failed resume-import job could still leave a usable-looking resumed-checkpoints bundle (missing the derived legacy baseline) behind. round1-candidates/round1-select/validate gate on !cancelled(), not needs.resume-import.result == 'success' (by design, documented elsewhere), so they would silently continue from that partial bundle, reintroducing the narrowed per-combo-incumbent safety-net gap for every non-LEGACY combo. FIXED by reordering 'Upload resumed checkpoints bundle' to be the LAST step in the job (after both legacy-baseline steps), so its existence now depends on the whole job's success up to that point. Added a regression test asserting the resumed-checkpoints upload step index is strictly greater than both legacy-baseline step indices AND equals steps.length-1. Targeted count: 163/163; npx tsc --noEmit clean; verify:fast clean.

3 MORE bot-flagged threads surfaced in a fresh copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot] pass immediately after the round-3 push, all directly enabled by round 3's new guarantee. (7th) checkpoint-init's 'Build round-0 checkpoint' step still had a RESUMED_COMBOS-conditioned jq fallback that degraded the legacy+legacy safety gate to a warning instead of hard-failing -- now provably unreachable/unsafe reasoning, because round 3's step-ordering fix plus the pre-existing needs.resume-import.result == success gate together guarantee that if checkpoint-init runs at all and legacy+legacy was resumed, the derived legacy+legacy baseline artifact MUST already exist. FIXED by removing RESUMED_COMBOS/jq fallback entirely; the step now ALWAYS exit 1s unconditionally when the shard is missing for a non-LEGACY combo. (8th) assertResumeCompatible's legacy-fallback branch deduped the REQUESTED trainSeeds/weapons strings via new Set(...) before comparing against the inferred panel, but the real evaluator (sweep-eval.ts's --train-seeds/--seeds/--weapons parsing, backed by winrate-sweep-args.ts's parseSeeds) preserves duplicates verbatim -- a fresh leg requesting e.g. '1,1,2' genuinely executes seed 1 twice and persists a duplicate row, so deduping the request before comparing silently accepted a request whose fresh execution would NOT match the imported duplicate-free panel. FIXED by rejecting duplicate seeds and duplicate/empty weapon entries in the requested string outright (fail closed) for the legacy-fallback path only; modern runInputs-present checkpoints unaffected. Added 3 new tests in sweep-round-plan.test.ts proving the fix is load-bearing (each shows the DEDUPED request would have otherwise matched the inferred panel). (9th) the stale ai-sweep-workflow.test.ts test codifying the now-removed RESUMED_COMBOS graceful-degrade behavior as correct was replaced with two new tests asserting the hard-fail-unconditionally behavior and that if-no-artifact-found:warn is display-only. Verified together: targeted count 167/167; npx tsc --noEmit clean; verify:fast clean; verify:pr-prereqs clean.

10th bot-flagged thread surfaced in a fresh copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot] pass after CI settled on the round-4 push (all 13 prior threads independently confirmed isResolved=true via GraphQL re-query first). assertResumeCompatible never bound the checkpoint PAYLOAD to the combo/round SLOT the workflow selected it for -- the resume-import job's 'Select latest compatible checkpoint' step only trusted the search-checkpoint-${r}-${COMBO}.json ARTIFACT FILENAME (looping over $COMBO/$r), then called round-plan.ts --mode resume-check without ever passing the expected combo or round. assertResumeCompatible checked metadata (schemaVersion/floorId/budgetMs/maxFrames/stage/runnerOs/nodeVersion/packageLockHash via assertShardCompatible) and run-input semantics (trainSeeds/weapons/secondary) but never compared checkpoint.combo or checkpoint.round against anything -- a mislabeled artifact (wrong combo, or a round exceeding the tier being imported) would pass every existing check and either fail confusingly much later, or silently resume MORE completed optimization than requested. FIXED by adding required combo/round fields to ResumeExpectedProvenance, checked FIRST in assertResumeCompatible (before the existing metadata/run-input checks) so a mislabeled artifact fails fast with an unambiguous error. Reused the CLI's existing generic --combo/--round flags (already used by init/plan/select modes) for --mode resume-check rather than adding new flag names -- both now required for that mode. ai-sweep.yml's resume-check invocation now maps the tier name it already loops over to the exact round number that tier implies (r3->3, r2->2, r1->1, init->0) via an inline case statement and passes --combo "$COMBO" --round "$EXPECT_ROUND". 4 new tests: combo-mismatch rejection, round-mismatch rejection, combo/round checked before other provenance fields, plus a workflow-level test asserting the exhaustive tier->round mapping and the --combo/--round invocation shape. Targeted count: 167 -> 171; npx tsc --noEmit clean; verify:fast clean; verify:pr-prereqs clean.

11th bot-flagged thread surfaced in a fresh copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot] pass after CI settled on the round-5 push (all 14 prior threads independently confirmed isResolved=true via GraphQL re-query first), at round-plan.ts:507. inferRunInputsFromCheckpoint derived a legacy checkpoint's implicit TRAIN panel by filtering checkpoint.rows on combo === checkpoint.incumbentCombo && configId === checkpoint.incumbentConfigId. For a non-LEGACY combo initialized WITHOUT a legacyBaseline these incumbent* fields equal the checkpoint's own combo/base-config, so this was correct there -- but initCheckpoint's legacyBaseline branch (used for every non-LEGACY combo evaluated against the fixed LEGACY safety-gate incumbent) forcibly sets incumbentCombo/incumbentConfigId to the SEPARATE LEGACY combo/base-config, a DIFFERENT combo/config than the checkpoint's own. Inference was therefore deriving a non-LEGACY checkpoint's own train panel from the LEGACY incumbent's rows instead of its own combo's rows. A malformed checkpoint whose own combo was evaluated on a narrow/wrong panel (e.g. seeds 1-24) while carrying a rectangular LEGACY incumbent panel (e.g. seeds 1-80) would have silently had its own panel inferred as 1-80, later mixing incomparable narrow (own) and wide (incumbent) totals as one train run. FIXED by deriving the checkpoint's OWN base config id independently via configId(baseConfigForCombo(parseComboId(checkpoint.combo))) -- which --stage search-baseline always uses for round-0 base rows regardless of the combo -- and filtering rows by combo === checkpoint.combo && configId === ownBaseConfigId, never the incumbent* fields. Extracted the duplicate-check/rectangular-check logic into a shared derivePanel(rows, panelLabel) closure, reused for both the checkpoint's own panel and (when checkpoint.incumbentCombo !== checkpoint.combo, i.e. a legacyBaseline was supplied) its separate LEGACY incumbent panel, which is now ALSO derived and required to match the own-combo panel EXACTLY (same sorted trainSeeds, same sorted weapons) -- a combo and its safety-gate incumbent evaluated on different train spaces are not comparable. 4 new tests in sweep-round-plan.test.ts: matching own/incumbent panels correctly infer from the OWN panel; seed-count mismatch rejected; same-seed-count-different-weapon-set mismatch rejected; a ragged/non-rectangular OWN panel is rejected even when the incumbent's panel alone would be clean (proving the own-panel proof runs independently). One pre-existing test's regex (/duplicate baseline row/) was updated to /duplicate own base config .* row/ to match derivePanel's now panel-labeled error text. Targeted count: 171 -> 175; npx tsc --noEmit clean; verify:fast clean.

12th bot-flagged thread surfaced in a fresh copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot] pass after CI settled on the round-6 push (all 15 prior threads independently confirmed isResolved=true via GraphQL re-query first, plus a distinct mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED-despite-mergeable diagnosis: a still-in_progress 'copilot' check-run, not a merge-gate/thread issue). Finding: assertResumeCompatible neutralizes workflowSha before delegating to assertShardCompatible (copying the checkpoint's own value into the comparison object) so an exact-match on GITHUB_SHA can never permanently block resume once the workflow file has since changed -- but packageLockHash (a hash of the ENTIRE package-lock.json) was still checked for strict equality via that same assertShardCompatible call. The bot confirmed the actual target run 29786216369's head commit used a package-lock.json that differs from this branch's by a routine fast-uri patch-version bump and a brace-expansion dev-marker change -- both incidental transitive/dev-dependency churn, not anything that touches simulation/runtime code. Since ANY dependency bump anywhere in the repo changes the whole-file hash, this meant the resume feature, exactly as built, could NEVER actually resume the specific run (29786216369) it exists to recover -- it would always fail closed on packageLockHash and silently fall back fresh, defeating the feature's stated purpose while still technically 'working' for a hypothetical same-lockfile future cancellation. Per rule #11 (never weaken an explicit human requirement -- 'reuse the existing strict provenance checks' -- without asking first), this was escalated to the human directly (not unilaterally decided) with 4 options; human selected: neutralize packageLockHash the SAME way workflowSha already is (informational only, not equality-gated), accepting the identical trade-off already made for workflowSha. FIXED by extending the existing neutralization pattern: assertResumeCompatible now copies checkpoint.meta.packageLockHash into the comparison object alongside workflowSha before calling assertShardCompatible; normalizeResumedCheckpoint (which re-stamps an ACCEPTED resumed checkpoint's workflowSha to the current run's value so later same-run checks in applyRoundResult/aggregate-shards.ts don't reject it) now ALSO re-stamps packageLockHash for the identical reason. Docstrings on both functions and the two ai-sweep.yml comment blocks describing the compatibility contract were updated to document packageLockHash as informational, matching workflowSha's existing treatment, and to record the concrete fast-uri/brace-expansion example as the motivating case. 6 tests updated/added in sweep-round-plan.test.ts: the pre-existing 'throws on packageLockHash mismatch' test was converted to 'does NOT throw' (mirroring the existing workflowSha test); a new 'still fails closed... even when packageLockHash ALSO differs' test (mirrors the existing workflowSha equivalent); a new 'still fails closed... even when BOTH workflowSha and packageLockHash differ' test; and normalizeResumedCheckpoint gained 3 new tests (re-stamps packageLockHash alone; re-stamps both together; re-stamps -- is NOT a no-op -- when packageLockHash alone differs even though workflowSha matches). Targeted count: 175 -> 180; npx tsc --noEmit clean; verify:fast clean; verify:pr-prereqs clean.

13th bot-flagged thread surfaced in a fresh copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot] pass after CI settled on the round-7 push (all 16 prior threads independently confirmed isResolved=true or awaiting the async reconciler via GraphQL re-query first), at round-plan.ts:1171. Finding: applyRoundResult's infraIncomplete guard (added earlier in this session's arc) correctly freezes bestConfigId/bestScore/steps/converged when some of a round's planned candidates never produced a shard (an infra failure, not a search dead-end) -- but its FINAL return statement unconditionally advanced the checkpoint's round field to Math.max(round, checkpoint.round) regardless of infraIncomplete. This produced a 'half-updated' checkpoint: search STATE correctly stayed frozen at the prior round's values, but the round LABEL falsely claimed the new round was complete. Because checkpoint.round is the ONLY place round-plan.ts checks an EXACT (not >=) equality -- assertResumeCompatible's combo/round binding (round-6's 10th-thread fix) -- and because ai-sweep.yml's resume-import job always uploads/renames artifacts as search-checkpoint-rN-<combo>.json based on the JOB's own hardcoded --round N flag (never the checkpoint's true completeness), a NEW dispatch whose rounds input EXACTLY matched an infra-incomplete checkpoint's (falsely-advanced) round would pass assertResumeCompatible's check and resume/validate directly against permanently-incomplete round-N search data -- the missing candidates would never be retried, since the resumed checkpoint is renamed to search-checkpoint-init-* and fed through round1..N's plan/select steps, each of which no-ops via the checkpoint.round >= round early-exit. (For rounds > N the extra round's own plan step is NOT gated at N, so planCandidates naturally retries the missing candidates there -- the bug is narrower than 'always broken': only the rounds === N exact-match resume case was silently unsafe.) FIXED with a one-line, minimal change: round-plan.ts:1171 now reads `round: infraIncomplete ? checkpoint.round : Math.max(round, checkpoint.round)`, deliberately reusing the EXISTING assertResumeCompatible combo/round strict-equality mechanism rather than adding a new field -- an infra-incomplete round's checkpoint now simply retains an OLDER round value, which will correctly mismatch its filename-implied tier on any future resume attempt, triggering the existing 'artifact appears mislabeled' rejection and falling back to the next-older genuinely-complete tier per resume-import's existing tier-scan loop. Manually traced single- and multi-round infra-incomplete chains (including 3 consecutive infra-incomplete rounds correctly self-healing all the way back to init). Docstring addenda added to both applyRoundResult (explaining the round-field implication) and assertResumeCompatible's existing COMBO/ROUND BINDING section (cross-referencing that this same check now ALSO guards against infra-incomplete rounds, not just mislabeled artifacts). 3 new tests in sweep-round-plan.test.ts: infra-incomplete round does NOT bump checkpoint.round (stays at prior value); a genuinely-complete round DOES advance round normally (control case proving the guard is targeted); and an end-to-end integration test proving an infra-incomplete round-2 checkpoint correctly fails assertResumeCompatible for the r2 tier it would be uploaded under while still validating cleanly against the r1 tier it genuinely completed -- composing the 13th fix with the existing 10th-thread combo/round check. Targeted count: 180 -> 183; npx tsc --noEmit clean; verify:fast clean; verify:pr-prereqs clean.
